title: What happens if you do not brush your teeth for a year

paragraphs: If you stop oral hygiene, the balance between helpful bacteria and harmful pathobionts in your mouth quickly breaks down.

Within just a few days, harmful bacteria multiply and create a sticky layer called dental plaque. This plaque irritates your gums, which can cause bleeding and inflammation, an early stage of disease called gingivitis. Within a month, the bacteria produce strong acids that eat away at tooth enamel and create painful cavities. If left untreated for several months, gingivitis worsens into periodontitis, which damages soft gum tissue and causes gums to pull away from your teeth.

After a year without cleaning, chronic infection destroys the underlying bone and causes teeth to wobble and fall out. Even worse, damaged gums allow harmful bacteria to enter your bloodstream. From there, these microbes can travel through the body and worsen serious health conditions, including heart disease, diabetes, and memory disorders like Alzheimer’s.

paragraphs: Your mouth needs daily cleaning to stay healthy. If you stop brushing and flossing, bad bacteria grow very fast.

In just a few days, sticky plaque covers your teeth, and your gums bleed and swell. This early stage is called gingivitis. After a month,  the bacteria break down tooth enamel and form cavities. If you ignore your teeth for a year, the infection gets much worse. Your gums pull away, the bone holding your teeth shrinks, and your teeth can fall out. Even worse, bad bacteria can get into your blood and cause serious health problems in your heart, kidneys, and brain.
Brushing twice a day stops these dangerous bugs and protects your whole body.

paragraphs: Brushing your teeth every day keeps your mouth healthy. If you stop cleaning your mouth, bad bacteria grow very fast. In a few days, your gums start to bleed and hurt.

After a month, the bugs make holes in your teeth. We call these holes cavities. If you go a full year without brushing, your teeth can fall out. Also, the bacteria can get into your blood and make your heart, brain, and body sick.
Brushing two times a day keeps your mouth clean, saves your teeth, and helps your body stay strong and happy.
